papers.title: Rational High-Throughput Screening of Cocrystals: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework Based on Morgan Fingerprints and Cross-Attention.
papers.abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high blindness in traditional screening methods, insufficient granularity of feature representation, and poor interpretability of existing machine learning prediction models in the field of cocrystal research and development, we propose a cocrystal prediction method based on Morgan fingerprints and the cross-attention mechanism. First, a high-quality cocrystal data set is constructed, and Morgan fingerprints are employed to characterize molecular structures. Subsequently, a fingerprint-driven cross-attention model is developed to capture the feature interactio
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that predicts cocrystal formation by combining Morgan fingerprints with a cross-attention mechanism. They built a curated cocrystal dataset and showed the model captures molecular feature interactions while providing interpretability, aiming to reduce the trial-and-error nature of traditional cocrystal screening.

papers.title: Deep learning of tautomer stability from crystallographic proton positions.
papers.abstract: Tautomerism plays a central role in molecular recognition, physicochemical properties, and chemical reactivity, yet rapid identification of stable tautomeric states remains a persistent challenge in molecular design and structure-based drug discovery. Quantum-mechanical approaches are often too computationally demanding for library-scale application, while rule-based and 3D-dependent machine-learning methods remain limited in either transferability or throughput. Here, we show that experimentally resolved hydrogen positions in the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) provide a powerful large-sc
papers.summary: The authors trained a deep learning model on experimentally resolved hydrogen positions from the Cambridge Structural Database to predict stable tautomeric states of molecules. This approach offers a fast, transferable alternative to quantum-mechanical calculations and rule-based methods, potentially enabling tautomer screening at library scale for drug discovery.

papers.title: AIDrugDesigner: a web server for drug-like molecules generation and optimization.
papers.abstract: Designing molecules with predefined properties remains a critical yet challenging task in drug discovery. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated strong potential in accelerating the identification of novel compounds with desired properties and activities. However, the implementation and running of these models often present difficulties due to varying environments and the requisite for additional coding competencies.
papers.summary: AIDrugDesigner is a web server that packages deep learning models for generating and optimizing drug-like molecules behind a user-friendly interface, removing the need for coding or environment setup. It aims to make generative molecular design accessible to medicinal chemists and other non-computational researchers.

papers.title: FuTCM-PDD: a multi-level information fusion framework integrating KAN modeling and AutoML for phenotype-based drug discovery from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.abstract: Phenotype-based drug discovery has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in first-in-class drug development and higher clinical translation rates. Chinese Materia Medica (CMM), with its emphasis on properties and efficacies, provides a unique framework for phenotype-oriented therapeutic discovery. We developed an AI-driven framework, FuTCM-PDD, that integrates CMMs, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, CMM efficacies, and CMM properties to enable phenotype-based drug discovery. For drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) m
papers.summary: FuTCM-PDD is an AI framework that fuses multi-level information (compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, and Traditional Chinese Medicine properties/efficacies) to support phenotype-based drug discovery. It uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for drug-target interaction prediction combined with AutoML, aiming to bridge TCM knowledge with modern phenotype-driven therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Physical priors improve performance of structure-based binding affinity models.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug discovery is a widely used paradigm for the rational design of novel small molecule therapeutics. However, the benefits conferred by the use of structural information has seen limited adoption in machine learning, where ligand-only ("2D") models are still the industry standard for molecular property or binding affinity prediction. Structure-based ("3D") ML models for binding-affinity prediction promise to present a clear advantage, but have not yet overtaken existing 2D models. Here, we show that physics-based priors can improve predictive performance of structure-based mo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint demonstrates that incorporating physics-based priors into structure-based machine learning models improves their ability to predict small molecule binding affinities. The authors argue that such physical priors help 3D models overcome limitations that have kept them from outperforming ligand-only 2D models. This work suggests a path toward more accurate structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Hit selection using SSMD-based machine learning performance metrics in high-throughput screening assays.
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening (HTS) assays are central to early-stage drug discovery but are often limited by extreme data sparsity, as primary screens typically use only a single replicate per test substance. This sparsity makes conventional machine-learning performance metrics, such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), difficult to estimate empirically because they require adequately sized labeled samples. Here, we introduce a model-based framework that derives these classification metrics from the strictly standardized mean difference
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This paper introduces a model-based framework that estimates conventional machine-learning classification metrics (sensitivity, specificity, AUROC) from the strictly standardized mean difference (SSMD) in high-throughput screening assays. The approach addresses the extreme data sparsity of primary screens, where typically only one replicate per test substance is available, making empirical estimation of these metrics difficult. This enables more reliable hit selection in early-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses reveal VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking environmental bisphenol A exposure to MASH-HCC progression.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC) is an increasingly important subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma, and environmental contaminants have been proposed as potential contributors to its progression. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in metabolic dysfunction and liver injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking BPA exposure to MASH-HCC remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed an integrated framework combining transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis,
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with network analysis and experimental validation to identify VIPR1 as a potential molecular link between bisphenol A (BPA) exposure and the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC). The findings suggest that environmental BPA exposure may promote liver cancer progression through VIPR1-mediated mechanisms, highlighting a gene-environment interaction relevant to liver disease.

papers.title: From Glycan Biology to Drug Candidates: An Integrated Sialylation Niche Index and AI-Guided Therapeutic Framework for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) responds poorly (<20%) to immune checkpoint blockade. Since sialylation suppresses anti-tumour immunity through Siglec signalling independently of the PD-L1/PD-1 axis, we mapped its prognostic landscape in HNSCC by integrating prognostic modelling, molecular subtyping, and AI-guided drug discovery. Methods: Transcriptomic data from seven GEO cohorts and TCGA-HNSC (n = 501) were analysed with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium. The Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) was built in TCGA-HNSC from 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations (nomi
papers.summary: This study developed a Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma by integrating transcriptomic data from multiple cohorts with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium, using 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations. The authors then applied AI-guided drug discovery to identify potential therapeutic candidates targeting the sialylation pathway, motivated by its role in suppressing anti-tumour immunity independently of PD-L1/PD-1.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Diversity of Marine-Derived Streptomyces Natural Products: Integrating Genome Mining, Multi-Omics, and Translational Drug Discovery Strategies.
papers.abstract: Marine-derived Streptomyces are among the most prolific producers of structurally diverse and biologically active natural products. Adaptation to unique marine environments, including deep-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangrove ecosystems, marine invertebrates, and hypersaline habitats, has promoted the evolution of specialized biosynthetic systems capable of generating a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites. These metabolites include polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides (NRPs), ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), terpenoids, alkaloids, and hybrid
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how marine-derived Streptomyces bacteria produce diverse natural products, highlighting how their adaptation to extreme marine environments drives the evolution of specialized biosynthetic pathways. It integrates genome mining, multi-omics approaches, and translational drug discovery strategies to uncover and develop these compounds as potential therapeutics.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3353 compounds and prioritized candidate ligands that remain stably bound to the mutant receptor, offering a computational pipeline for targeting resistant ERα variants.

papers.title: TRPM8 virtual screening: the essential role of target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions.
papers.abstract: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein confo
papers.summary: This study establishes the first comprehensive structure-based virtual screening benchmark for the TRPM8 ion channel, a therapeutic target for pain and inflammation. It compares classical docking scoring functions, generic machine-learning scoring functions, and target-specific ML models across multiple TRPM8 protein conformations. The key finding is that target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions substantially improve virtual screening performance for this challenging ion channel target.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically assesses the current state of molecular docking studies applied to natural products, highlighting widespread methodological variability and the absence of standardized guidelines. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches and offers practical recommendations for improving rigor. The work serves as a methodological reference for researchers conducting or evaluating docking studies in natural-product drug discovery.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: The authors propose a retrieval-guided transfer learning framework to predict drug-target binding affinity for Ebola, a disease with scarce experimental affinity data. The method uses BindingDB interactions as a source domain, selecting relevant source data via random sampling and compound- or protein-similarity retrieval before transferring to the Ebola target task. This addresses the practical challenge of building DTA models for neglected or emerging pathogens with limited labeled data.

papers.title: Confidence-Gated Triage: Coupling Drug-Target Affinity and ADME-T Predictions to Prioritise Compounds for Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally expensive, so the compounds entering them must be chosen well. The present study proposes CADT, a confidence-gated affinity-ADME-T docking-triage cascade that decides which compounds are worth docking. Methods: The gate combines an ensemble estimate of drug-target affinity with its epistemic uncertainty and an applicability-domain check. Predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADME-T) developability is added as a soft flag. All components were trained on openly lice
papers.summary: The authors present CADT, a triage cascade that uses an ensemble drug-target affinity model with uncertainty estimates and an applicability-domain check, plus ADME-T developability predictions, to decide which compounds are worth the cost of molecular docking. The goal is to filter large compound libraries so that expensive docking and molecular dynamics are reserved for the most promising candidates.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation-Guided Discovery of Novel Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint is a key therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy, but small-molecule inhibition remains challenging due to its shallow and dynamic interaction interface. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided workflow to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface. Methods: A combined computational and experimental approach was established. A support vector regression-genetic algorithm (SVR-GA) model was trained on a dataset of 1385 known PD-L1
papers.summary: This study develops an AI-guided workflow combining machine learning (SVR-GA) and molecular simulation to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface for cancer immunotherapy. The approach addresses the challenge of the shallow, dynamic PD-1/PD-L1 interaction interface by integrating computational prediction with experimental validation.

papers.title: Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in Cancer Drug Discovery: Promise, Challenges, and Emerging Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Oncologic drug development is lengthy (~14 years) and expensive (~1.2 billion USD) with low clinical trial success rates (4.1%). Big data and artificial intelligence (AI) are widely proposed as tools to address these challenges. In this review, we examine the current performance and future potential of big data and AI applied to preclinical discovery and development, clinical trials, and the regulatory approval process. We first examine the data foundation required for effective AI, including data harmonization, data commons, and analytical tools. We then assess preclinical applications spanni
papers.summary: This review examines how big data and AI are being applied across the cancer drug development pipeline, from preclinical discovery through clinical trials and regulatory approval. It highlights the data infrastructure requirements (harmonization, data commons, analytical tools) needed for effective AI, while assessing both current performance and remaining challenges in a field where drug development takes ~14 years and costs ~$1.2 billion with only 4.1% clinical trial success rates.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict inhibitors of coagulation factor XIIa, a target in the contact activation pathway. Using IC50 data from ChEMBL, the authors built ensemble models with scaffold-aware validation, aiming to support drug discovery for contact-system-associated processes.

papers.title: An AI-Assisted Workflow for Rapid Prioritization of FDA-Approved Drugs as HDAC3 Inhibitor Candidates for Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation through histone acetylation plays a critical role in gene expression and cancer progression. Because of its pivotal role in chromatin remodeling, Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) has become a promising therapeutic target. In this study, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven strategy was utilized to prioritize potential HDAC3 inhibitors among FDA-approved compounds to accelerate drug repurposing for cancer therapy. Existing HDAC3 inhibitors were identified in the BindingDB and were used to develop a machine learning (ML) model trained on the most potent inhibitors to identif
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning workflow to screen FDA-approved drugs for potential HDAC3 inhibition, aiming to accelerate drug repurposing for cancer therapy. The model was trained on known potent HDAC3 inhibitors from BindingDB and used to prioritize candidates among existing approved compounds. The approach demonstrates how AI can streamline early-stage drug discovery by repurposing existing therapeutics.

papers.title: An Explainable Machine Learning-Based QSAR Framework for Predicting Thrombin Inhibitory Activity.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Public thrombin bioactivity records contain heterogeneous endpoints, replicate measurements, related chemical series, and potentially reactive compounds that may bias quantitative structure-activity relationship models. In this study, we developed an explainable, assay-aware, and leakage-safe machine learning framework for predicting thrombin-inhibitory activity. Methods: Exact Ki and IC50 records for human thrombin (CHEMBL204) were standardized, converted to pActivity, and aggregated using predefined criteria. The final dataset comprised 5189 unique compounds represente
papers.summary: This paper presents an explainable machine learning QSAR framework for predicting thrombin inhibitory activity, addressing common pitfalls like heterogeneous endpoints, replicate measurements, and data leakage. Using 5,189 unique compounds from ChEMBL204, the authors standardize and aggregate Ki/IC50 data to build a leakage-safe, assay-aware model. The framework emphasizes interpretability, making predictions more trustworthy for drug discovery applications.

papers.title: AI-Powered Marine Drug Discovery: A Putative Dual c-Met/VEGFR2 Lead Candidate for Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Deep Learning and Multiscale Simulation.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. The c-Met and VEGFR2 pathways synergistically drive HCC progression. Marine natural products offer chemically diverse drug reservoirs; however, conventional activity-guided isolation faces labor intensity, low throughput, and frequent compound rediscovery, limiting marine drug development.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning combined with multiscale molecular simulation to mine marine natural products for a compound that simultaneously inhibits c-Met and VEGFR2, two kinases that cooperatively drive hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors identify a putative dual-target lead candidate, offering an AI-driven alternative to slow, low-throughput activity-guided isolation in marine drug discovery.

papers.title: Multi-target cell membrane chromatography intelligent screening strategy and its application in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: • MCMC-ISW enables paradigm shift from single-to-multi-target biomimetic screening via CMC and AI-driven recognition and analysis. • Three pathways (mixed membranes, arrays, organoids) enable parallel and physiological multi-target screening. • Whole-genome pan-GPCR library provides target coverage and resource for multi-target screening and receptor-ligand studies. • Platform validates multi-target synergy of TCM formulas and accelerates hit discovery from herbal and compound libraries. • MCMC-ISW offers methodological support and tool references for complex systems and advancing multi-target
papers.summary: This paper introduces MCMC-ISW, a multi-target cell membrane chromatography platform that combines biomimetic screening with AI-driven recognition to move beyond single-target drug screening. It supports three parallel screening pathways (mixed membranes, arrays, and organoids) and includes a whole-genome pan-GPCR library for broad target coverage. The platform was applied to validate multi-target synergy in traditional Chinese medicine formulas and to accelerate hit discovery from herbal and compound libraries.

papers.title: AlloPool is a deep learning framework that infers protein allostery from molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed protein structure prediction and design. However, protein function is governed not only by static structures but also by the conformational dynamics that allow proteins to access distinct functional states. Predicting these dynamic transitions, central to many biological processes, remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-resolution experimental data, which limits the training of machine-learning models for dynamic and energetic property prediction. Here, we present AlloPool, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that in
papers.summary: AlloPool is a graph neural network framework that predicts protein allostery—how binding at one site affects function at a distant site—by learning from molecular dynamics simulations. It addresses the scarcity of experimental data on protein conformational dynamics by leveraging simulation-derived training data. The tool aims to make dynamic and energetic property prediction more tractable for protein function analysis.

papers.title: Skin Aging: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic and Technological Innovations.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex, pervasive biological process that causes irreversible declines in function across organ systems. The skin, the body's largest organ, interfaces directly with the external environment and undergoes aging driven by intrinsic (chronological) and extrinsic (environmental) factors, which result in functional deterioration and greater susceptibility to related disorders. Although numerous anti-aging strategies have been investigated, relatively few specifically target the skin. This review delineates the principal phenotypes and underlying mechanisms of skin aging. Phenotypic hal
papers.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on skin aging, distinguishing intrinsic chronological aging from extrinsic environmental damage and describing the resulting cellular and molecular phenotypes. It also surveys emerging therapeutic and technological strategies aimed specifically at countering skin aging, an area where targeted interventions remain relatively scarce.

papers.title: FOXC1 drives lung cancer metastasis and functions as a target for AI-enabled anti-metastatic drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of treatment failure and death. Forkhead box C1 (FOXC1) promotes cancer progression, but its definitive mechanism in lung cancer metastasis and druggable potential remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify the mechanism and develop a FOXC1-targeted inhibitor.
papers.summary: This study identifies the transcription factor FOXC1 as a key driver of lung cancer metastasis and demonstrates that it can be targeted therapeutically. The authors use AI-enabled drug discovery to identify a FOXC1 inhibitor, providing a proof-of-concept for anti-metastatic treatment in lung cancer.

papers.title: Transforming Nanomaterials Development with Artificial Intelligence Techniques.
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into various scientific fields is reshaping traditional methodologies, and nanotechnology is no exception. This article explores the transformative impact of AI on nanotechnology, a domain focused on manipulating matter at atomic and molecular scales to develop novel materials with tailored properties. Historically, the discovery and optimization of nanomaterials relied on labor-intensive trial-and-error methods, often taking years to yield practical results. We examine how recent advances in AI particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning,
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, is transforming nanotechnology by replacing slow trial-and-error nanomaterial discovery with data-driven prediction and optimization. It surveys AI applications across nanomaterial design, property prediction, and synthesis, arguing that these methods can dramatically accelerate development timelines.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery is essential to mitigate the high attrition rates and capital-intensive nature of traditional pharmaceutical research. Deep learning (DL) has catalyzed a paradigm shift, offering unprecedented computational capabilities to accelerate this process. This review systematically summarizes advancements in DL methodologies for drug discovery. First, the critical data foundations, Molecular Representation Learning, and core architectures underpinning artificial intelligence (AI)-driven therapeutics are elucidated, with a particular emphasis on the evolution of generative AI f
papers.summary: This review surveys how deep learning is transforming drug discovery, covering molecular representation learning, core neural network architectures, and generative AI approaches. It highlights how these computational methods can reduce the high attrition rates and costs of traditional pharmaceutical R&D.

papers.title: Network biology to artificial intelligence: building the next generation of predictive drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery remains constrained by high attrition rates, prolonged timelines, and limited ability to translate molecular insights into effective therapies. Although reductionist approaches targeting individual molecules have delivered transformative medicines, successful patient-centric treatment remains a major challenge. Furthermore, increasing evidence demonstrates that therapeutic outcomes emerge from complex, dynamic, and context-dependent biological networks. Systems biology has provided a framework to understand these interactions, yet its predictive capability has been limited by bi
papers.summary: This review argues that drug discovery's high failure rates stem from reductionist single-target approaches that ignore the complex, context-dependent nature of biological networks. It proposes integrating systems biology with artificial intelligence to build predictive models that better capture network-level therapeutic effects and improve translation to patient outcomes.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction is essential for computational drug discovery, yet existing deep learning methods typically employ a single globally trained model that fails to adapt to individual query samples. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end framework that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs-samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels under manifold smoothness constraints-and integrates them via a semi-supervised graph convolutional network (GCN). For each query, we automatically construct a graph where nodes represent protein-ligand pairs and edges
papers.summary: The authors introduce RA-PLA, a retrieval-augmented framework that improves protein-ligand binding affinity prediction by identifying 'hard' training pairs whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels and incorporating them through a semi-supervised graph convolutional network. This allows the model to adapt to individual query samples rather than relying on a single globally trained predictor, potentially improving accuracy in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in non-small cell lung cancer: transforming diagnosis, treatment, and prognostic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by profound biological heterogeneity, frequently leading to late-stage diagnosis, recurrence, or metastasis. Conventional clinical pathways heavily depend on subjective visual interpretations, invasive tissue biopsies, and experience-based medical models that constrain individualized precision medicine. Identifying noninvasive, cross-scale tools for whole-disease-course assessment is critical for optimizing clinical decision-making and survival outcomes. This review critically synthesizes recent research progress and core algorithmic applicat
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying artificial intelligence to non-small cell lung cancer across diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. It highlights how AI can address limitations of conventional clinical pathways, such as subjective interpretation and invasive biopsies, by enabling noninvasive, cross-scale assessment for precision medicine.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in experimental and clinical in vitro analysis: applications, limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into in vitro analyses represents a transformative shift in laboratory medicine, diagnostics, and pharmaceutical research. Traditional in vitro methods, from cell culture assays to high-throughput screening, rely on manual interpretation and conventional statistics. Machine and deep learning now automate image analysis, improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery, and enhance quality control. Convolutional neural networks and predictive models have reported specialist-level performance in cell segmentation, biomarker detection, and patholog
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly machine and deep learning, is being integrated into in vitro laboratory analyses such as cell culture assays and high-throughput screening. It highlights applications in automating image analysis, improving diagnostic accuracy, accelerating drug discovery, and enhancing quality control, while also discussing current limitations and future directions.
